text:
incident-bot: PAGE: high error surface detected — elevated 429 + 503 rates from prod-west-1 over the last 3m. Alert threshold breached. paging: @Jamie (primary-oncall), @Priya (backup). dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/r/req-errors?region=prod-west-1 :rotating_light:

Jamie: saw the page, joining. quick check: are these user-facing 503s or internal proxy 503s?

Priya: looks like both. summary query I ran (Prom):
```promql
sum by (response_code) (rate(http_server_responses_total{env="prod",region="west-1"}[2m]))
```
results: spikes at 429 and 503, 429 concentrated on /v1/embeddings and /v1/generate routes.

Drew: throwing up the request queue depth and reject logs now. `kubectl logs -l app=gateway -n prod --since=10m | grep -E "429|503" | head -n 200`

Miriam: paging product & support threads — potential customer-facing impact, prepping a short blurb for support if hit. Tina, can you start triage in #support?

Tina (support): on it. will flag top affected tenants & open quick contact list.

Jamie: initial read — sudden traffic surge from one tenant group + a downstream KV cache flakiness causing cascading backpressure. Plan: 1) apply tenant-level soft QPS cap to noisy tenants 2) enable fast-fail feature-flag for non-essential routes 3) increase proxy worker count as temporary relief. doing steps in that order.

Carlos: adding runbook note: set tenant caps via admin service. API snippet:
```bash
# cap tenant T-123 to 200 r/s (soft, drops to 429)
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  https://admin.redwood.internal/tenants/T-123/caps \
  -d '{"qps_soft":200}'
```

Jamie: applying cap to top offenders now. hitting admin -> 200 r/s for T-123 and T-456. responses look OK: `{"status":"updated"}`

Priya: while Jamie does that, I'm flipping the feature flag that causes heavy embedding pre-filtering (non-critical). feature toggle command (FFS):
```bash
# toggle fast-fail for embedding prefilter
curl -X PATCH -H "Authorization: Bearer $FFS_TOKEN" \
  https://ff.redwood.internal/flags/embeddings-prefilter -d '{"enabled":false}'
```

Jamie: caps in place. immediate drop in per-tenant qps on dashboards. 429 rate for /v1/embeddings down ~60% in last 30s. 503s still elevated — looks like downstream cache is still failing under load.

Drew: scaling proxy workers by +2 replicas in prod-west-1, applying patch: `kubectl scale deploy/gateway --replicas=6 -n prod`. will monitor CPU and queue latency.

Miriam: support blurb drafted: "We're seeing elevated 429/503 errors affecting a subset of customers in US-West. Engineers are actively mitigating — temporary rate limits may be applied. We'll update in 15 minutes." sending now.

Tina (support): sent to affected accounts list (T-123, T-456, T-789). no high-severity customer replies yet, some automated alerts from partners.

Priya: monitoring short window summaries (Grafana panel) — metrics shifting: 429 down, 503 slowly trending down. attaching quick Prom snapshots: `sum(rate(http_server_responses_total{code=~"5..",env="prod"}[1m])) by (instance)` shows top 3 instances with errors: gw-3, gw-5, gw-8.

Jamie: suspected root cause is cache timeouts + retry storm from client SDK when getting 429s. next step: enable short-lived retry-backoff in the traffic proxy to reduce downstream retries. I'll patch runtime config:
```yaml
# proxy retry tuning
retry:
  enabled: true
  max_retries: 1
  backoff_ms: 300
```
Applying now.

Drew: runtime config applied on canary pods, watching for improved 503 counts.

incident-bot: note added to incident timeline: mitigation actions (tenant caps, feature-toggle, scale-up, retry-tuning). link: https://incidents.redwood.internal/INC-2022

Miriam: product asked for estimated impact window. based on current trends I'd say 15-30m to stabilize, subject to downstream cache recovery.

Carlos: created a short-lived dashboard panel focusing on request rejection rate by tenant: https://dash.redwood.internal/r/tenants-rejects?window=10m

Jamie: update — after caps + retry tuning + scale-up, 429s are now at baseline for most tenants, 503s dropped by 75% but still a tail at gw-8. I'm going to cordon gw-8 out of traffic for investigation: `kubectl annotate node/gw-8 maintenance=true` and drain if needed.

Priya: gating rollback of the embedding prefilter flag until we confirm stability. good to keep it off for now.

Tina (support): relaying to affected customers: "We've applied temporary limits and disabled a non-essential prefilter to reduce errors. We'll follow up when services are stable."

Drew: gw-8 cordoned, initiating deeper log capture. early signs point to resource exhaustion on that host (OOM events around spike time). opening a host-level alert to infra.

Miriam: product -> scheduled a postmortem call at +2h. we'll collect logs, timeline, and customer impact.

Jamie: current status summary for channel: 1) Mitigations applied: tenant caps, feature-flag off, proxy scale + retry tuning, cordoned faulty host. 2) Impact: majority of tenant 429s resolved, 503s largely mitigated; small tail remains while host is investigated. 3) Next steps: recover host or replace, continue monitoring, prepare postmortem.

Priya: will keep monitoring dashboards and notify when thresholds clear. if anything regresses ping @channel and we'll re-run mitigation. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: incident state updated -> under mitigation. record: 2223456789.
